steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Reagents
steps.instruction: Decontaminate surfaces and equipment to prevent RNA degradation.

substeps.instruction: Treat surfaces and equipment with RNase Away.
DEPC-treat alcohols and water used in the protocol; perform final dehydrating steps with undenatured ethanol.
Prepare 0.1% DEPC Solution: mix 999 ml deionized water with 1 ml DEPC Mix overnight, then autoclave in the morning.

steps.title: Collect and Fix Tissue
steps.instruction: Collect uterine wall samples from the lower uterine segment during cesarean delivery, after baby delivery but before placenta delivery and intravenous oxytocin application.

substeps.instruction: Identify the scarred area (e.g., via intraoperative ultrasound) and mark with cautery points; place uterotomy 1 cm above the scar.
Cut out a small piece of tissue containing both healthy myometrium and the scarred area.
Immediately cut samples to a size no thicker than 1 cm to ensure proper formalin and paraffin penetration.
Immerse samples in 4% neutral buffered formalin in an adequate vessel for 24-48 hours at room temperature.

steps.title: Dehydration and Paraffinization
steps.instruction: Process tissues using a Citadel 1000 system according to the following sequence:

substeps.instruction: 70% Ethanol: 3 hours
70% Ethanol: 1 hour
70% Ethanol: 1 hour
80% Ethanol: 1 hour
96% Ethanol: 1 hour
100% Ethanol: 1 hour
100% Ethanol: 1 hour
100% Ethanol: 1 hour
Chloroform: 1 hour
Chloroform: 2 hours
Paraffin: 2 hours
Paraffin: 3 hours

steps.title: Sectioning and Slide Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare tissue sections for laser microdissection.

substeps.instruction: Cool tissue blocks at 4°C for 1 hour to harden wax.
Fasten the cooled block into a rotary microtome block holder.
Trim the block at 20 µm thickness to expose the representative surface, then cut 5 µm thick slides.
Heat the rotary microtome water bath with deionized water to 36°C.
Mount unwrinkled sections on Superfrost Plus Langenbrick glass slides.
Dry sections overnight at 37°C in a heating cabinet (Heraeus Type 290).
Store slides at room temperature protected from light (or at 4°C if space permits).

steps.title: Staining and Identification
steps.instruction: Stain sections to identify regions of interest.

substeps.instruction: Perform Deparaffinization and Rehydration: Xylol (5 min x2), 96% Ethanol (2 min), 70% Ethanol (2 min), 50% Ethanol (2 min), Aqua dest. (2 min).

Perform H&E or Gomori-Trichrome staining: Boin Solution (30 min at 56°C), running tap water (5 min), Weigert's hematoxylin (10 min), running tap water (10 min), Trichrome Solution (25 min), 0.5% acetic acid (2 min), 0.5% acetic acid (1 min).
Dehydrate: 96% Ethanol (1 min), 100% Ethanol (2 min x2), Xylol (5 min x2).
Let sections air-dry; do not apply a cover glass.

steps.title: Laser Microdissection (LMD)
steps.instruction: Isolate the scarred area of interest using a laser microscope.

substeps.instruction: Immediately transfer the stained slide to the laser microscope or store in a sterile falcon tube at 4°C (do not freeze).
Place the slide into the holder specimen-side down.
Encircle the area of interest using the freehand point-to-point function.
Calculate the expected RNA amount based on area (µm2 * 5 µm thickness).
Set laser power to maximum to create a macroscopically visible marking.
Transfer the slide to a workbench decontaminated with RNA Zap.

steps.title: Tissue Recovery and Storage
steps.instruction: Scratch the microdissected tissue into a stabilization buffer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube with 150 µl Proteinase K Buffer (PKD) and 1 µl Stabilizer Reagent (use 20 µl Stabilizer per 1 mg of tissue).
Using a clean scalpel and spatula (decontaminated with UV or RNAZap), scratch the marked area off the slide and transfer it into the buffer tube.
Store the tube at 4°C for up to 24 hours if necessary.
Once sufficient tissue is collected, freeze the sample at -20°C briefly, then thaw immediately before RNA extraction.

steps.title: RNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract RNA using the RNeasy MinElute kit with modified incubation times.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µl Proteinase K; mix carefully without vortexing.
Incubate at 56°C in an Eppendorf Thermomixer (with shaking) overnight (up to 24 hours).
Cool on ice for 3 min, then let rest at room temperature until the heating block reaches 80°C.
Centrifuge for 15 min at 20,000 x g (13,500 rpm).
Incubate the sample at 80°C for 15 minutes in the Thermomixer.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 ml tube without disturbing the pellet.
Add DNase Booster Buffer (approx. 16 µl, or 1/10th of total volume).
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min, flicking the tube every 3 minutes.
Add 10 µl DNase I stock solution; mix carefully without vortexing.
Add 320 µl Buffer RBC and mix thoroughly.
Add 720 µl 100% ethanol and mix carefully.
Transfer 650 µl of the sample to an RNeasy MinElute spin column; centrifuge for 15 s at 8000 x g (10,000 rpm).
Transfer the remaining sample to the same column; centrifuge for 15 s at 10,000 rpm and discard flowthrough.
Wash: Add 500 µl Buffer RPE, centrifuge for 15 s at 8000 x g (10,000 rpm), discard flowthrough.
Wash: Add 500 µl Buffer RPE, close lid, centrifuge for 2 min at 8000 x g (10,000 rpm), discard flowthrough and collection tube.
Dry: Place column in a new 2 ml collection tube, open lid, and centrifuge at full speed for 5 min. Discard collection tube.
Elute: Place column in a new 1.5 ml tube, add 14–30 µl RNase-free water directly to the membrane, close lid, and centrifuge for 1 min at full speed.

steps.title: RNA Quality Control (Bio-Analyzer)
steps.instruction: Analyze RNA concentration and quality using a Bio-Analyzer chip.

substeps.instruction: Clean the electrode: Pipette 350 µl RNase ZAP-water (1:1) into a well, close flap, wait 1 min, remove. Then apply 350 µl RNase-free water, close flap, wait 10s, and let evaporate for 10s with flap open.

Prepare gel-dye mix: Centrifuge 550 µl RNA-gel-matrix on a spin filter for 10 min at 1500 rcf. Aliquot 65 µl gel and store at 4°C. Vortex blue RNA dye, centrifuge, add 1 µl dye to 65 µl gel, vortex, and centrifuge for 10 min at 13,000 rcf.

Prime station: Place chip on priming station. Apply 9 µl gel-dye mix to G-well. Position plunger at 1 mL, close station, press syringe until held by clip, wait 30s, loosen clip, hold for 5s, and slowly draw back to 1 mL.
Load chip: Apply 9 µl gel-dye mix to the two G-wells with white backgrounds. Apply 5 µl RNA marker (green) to all 12 sample wells and the ladder well. Apply 1 µl ladder to the ladder well.
Load samples: Transfer 1 µl RNA sample to each of the 12 sample wells; fill empty wells with 1 µl RNA marker.
Vortex chip at 2400 rpm for 1 min.
Insert chip, enter sample descriptions, and run immediately (within 5 minutes). Use RNA 6000 Nano kit for 25-500 ng/µL or RNA 6000 Pico kit for 50-5,000 pg/µL.
Clean with H2O after measurement.

steps.title: Reverse Transcription (cDNA Synthesis)
steps.instruction: Convert RNA to cDNA using the BioRad iScript Synthesis Kit in an Eppendorf Mastercycler.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 20 µl reaction containing: up to 15 µl RNA eluate (corresponding to 1 µg RNA), 4 µl iScript primer mix (oligo dT and random primers), and nuclease-free water to reach 20 µl.
Centrifuge, cool down, and hold at 4°C.
Perform reverse transcription to obtain 20 µl of cDNA eluate (approx. 50 ng/µl).
Set up Sample-RT Control (RNA template + primer mix, no RT) and NTC control (RT + primer mix, no RNA template).
Aliquot cDNA and freeze at -20°C.

steps.title: qPCR Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform qPCR in Singleplex using Taqman probe technology in 96-well plates in an ABI 7500.

substeps.instruction: Load wells with: Taqman Universal PCR Mastermix (2X), Taqman Gene Expression Assay (10X), cDNA (<100 ng), and nuclease-free water.
Run qPCR protocol: Enzyme activation (10 min at 95°C), followed by 45 cycles of denaturation (15 sec at 95°C) and annealing/elongation (1 min at 60°C).
Run an interplate calibrator (cDNA or gDNA with a housekeeping gene) on each plate to detect variance.
Load plates using the sample maximization method: one gene per plate, mixing samples from different groups on the same plate.

steps.title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Prepare and run a 5% agarose gel for DNA analysis.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1X TAE Buffer: 20 ml TAE (50X) + 980 ml H2O.
Prepare gel: Weigh 5g agarose in 100 ml 1X TAE buffer. Dissolve in microwave at 560W until boiling. Cool to 50-60°C for approx. 10 min.
Add 10 µl ethydium bromide (1 µl per 10 mL gel) to the cooled solution; stir until liquid.
Pour gel without air bubbles, insert comb (0.5-1 cm from upper edge), and let harden for approx. 1 hour. Pour 1X TAE buffer over the gel and remove comb.
Load first pocket with 6 µl DNA ladder. Load further pockets with 6 µl mixture (5 µl PCR sample + 1 µl loading buffer).
Run for approx. 60 min at 5 volts per cm of gel length.
